screenshots.shows: JSONL editor at 2853x1428: full plugin toolbar (gear, Left panel Raw/Formatted with Formatted on, Right panel Raw/Formatted/Inspect/Off with Inspect on, Level Debug, Target (All), empty Filter, Total entries: 163, First entry: 5 hours 11 minutes ago, Most recent: less than a minute ago). Below it, formatted Rust-tracing log lines 91-132 from 2026-04-25 (usage_limits/http_server/log_watcher/notifications), line 115 caret-highlighted, and the Inspect overlay in the top-right corner showing that entry's pretty-printed JSON ("watching transcript", target ai_agent_dashboard_lib::log_watcher).

steps: Open a .jsonl produced by a Rust app using tracing's JSON subscriber in an IntelliJ-platform IDE (dark theme, e.g. the AI agent dashboard widget log). Each line should look like {"timestamp":"2026-04-25T12:05:27.786319Z","level":"DEBUG","fields":{"message":"watching transcript","path":"...","chat_id":"..."},"target":"ai_agent_dashboard_lib::log_watcher"}. Use about 163 entries with targets usage_limits, http_server, log_watcher and notifications, and messages like 'refresh request denied (inside floor)', 'event -> set', 'usage poll success', 'widget starting'.
In the plugin toolbar, set Left panel to Formatted and Right panel to Inspect, so the Inspect overlay floats in the top-right corner (its corner button shows a down arrow).
Set Level to Debug and Target to (All), and leave Filter empty. Timestamps should show relative time: first entry about 5 hours ago, most recent under a minute ago.

In the gear menu, turn soft wrap for the inspect pane on (the long path value wraps) and auto-resize inspect off (the bottom-left resize grip is visible). Keep italic target and Fields-level alignment, so the k=v fields line up in one column.

Scroll the formatted pane so lines 91-132 are visible and put the caret on line 115, the log_watcher 'watching transcript' entry for intellij-jsonl-extension, so the overlay shows its JSON (10 lines).
Widen the overlay to about 35% of the editor width and let its height fit the 10-line JSON.

Capture at 150% scaling (144 DPI) and crop tightly to the plugin's editor component: from the toolbar's gear icon at top-left down to the bottom of the editor, with no IDE tabs, tool windows or window chrome. The result is 2853x1428.

screenshots.shows: Cropped plugin editor toolbar (dark New UI), pane-selector section only. "Left panel:" has 3 icon buttons: Raw {}, Formatted (selected) and Inspect. "Right panel:" has 4: Raw {}, Formatted (disabled), Inspect (selected) and Off (X).

steps: Run the plugin in IntelliJ (runIde sandbox) with the dark New UI theme. The toolbar background is RGB (25,26,28), the same as main-large.png, toolbar-filter.png and toolbar-stats.png.

Open a .jsonl log of Rust tracing JSON lines, each shaped like {"timestamp": "...Z", "level": "DEBUG", "fields": {"message": ..., ...}, "target": "ai_agent_dashboard_lib::usage_limits"}. The content does not appear in this crop; use the same file as the main-large.png hero shot so the series stays consistent.

In the editor's toolbar, click the Formatted (lines) icon under "Left panel:" and the Inspect icon under "Right panel:". This is the default Left = Formatted, Right = Inspect. Formatted then shows as disabled in the Right group.
Do not hover any button, so no tooltip or hover highlight is captured.
Take a screenshot at the same display scale as main-large.png (native HiDPI, where the toolbar strip is 54 px tall).

Crop to the full toolbar height (54 px). Start about 17 px left of the "Left panel:" label, after the gear icon. End about 13 px past the Right group's Off (X) button, before "Level:". The Left group should now show only 2 buttons (Raw, Formatted), so the crop will be narrower than the old 550 px (roughly 505 px).
Save over docs/screenshots/toolbar-panels.png.

steps: Install the current plugin build in IntelliJ with the New UI dark theme and display scaling around 150%. The frame's search field is about 290 px wide against FILTER_WIDTH_PX = 200, which matches main-large.png's toolbar.

Open a .jsonl log of Rust tracing JSON lines, each with timestamp, level (TRACE/DEBUG/INFO), fields.message plus extra fields, and target values such as ai_agent_dashboard_lib::usage_limits, ::http_server, ::log_watcher and ::notifications. This is the same ai-agent-dashboard log family seen in main-large.png, so the JSONL split editor opens with its toolbar.
In the JSONL editor toolbar, leave the Level combo on "All".
Open the Target combo and pick ai_agent_dashboard_lib::usage_limits so the combo button shows that full target name.
Leave the Filter search field empty and unfocused.

Screenshot the toolbar row. Crop horizontally from just left of the "Level:" label to just past the right edge of the Filter search field, leaving out the pane selectors on the left and the "Total entries" stats on the right. Keep the full toolbar height (54 px, the same as the toolbar-panels.png and toolbar-stats.png crops).

screenshots.shows: Right-click popup over the Formatted pane, where "client=claude event=Stop" is selected on an "event -> set" line; the popup lists Filter by "client=claude event=Stop", a separator, and Copy Ctrl+C.

steps: Build and run the plugin in a sandbox IDE (runIde) that uses the same dark theme as the other screenshots in docs/screenshots.

Open a .jsonl log in Rust tracing JSON format. Each line is {timestamp, level, target, fields:{message, ...}}, from the AI agent dashboard (target ai_agent_dashboard_lib::...), the same log family as main.png. The file needs hook-event lines whose message is "event -> set" with fields client=claude, event=Stop / UserPromptSubmit / Notification and chat_id=intellij-jsonl-extension. It also needs usage_limits lines whose message is "usage poll success" with fields five_hour_raw=37.0 seven_day_raw=82.0. In the visible stretch, one usage-poll line sits between runs of event -> set lines.
Show the Formatted pane (Left panel = Formatted). Clear any Level, Target or text filter so the mixed hook-event and usage-poll lines are visible.
In the Formatted pane, drag-select the text "client=claude event=Stop" on an "event -> set ... event=Stop" line, the fourth visible line in the crop.
Right-click the selection so the viewer popup opens next to it, showing Filter by "client=claude event=Stop", a separator, and Copy Ctrl+C. Do not hover any item, so no row is highlighted.

Crop to a strip about 868x222 px at the same display scale as the original (line pitch about 32 px). The strip covers seven formatted lines. The left crop edge cuts off the gutter, line numbers, timestamp, level and target, so each line starts at its message ("event -> set" / " usage poll success"). The right edge cuts through the popup's right border, and the bottom edge sits just below the popup.

screenshots.shows: Cropped right-hand stats segment of the JSONL editor toolbar in a dark theme: "Total entries: 75", "First entry:  10 hours 32 minutes ago", "Most recent:  9 minutes ago" (relative-time mode, no tooltip showing)

steps: Run the plugin in a sandbox IDE (runIde) with a dark theme (the frame uses a dark New UI-style theme). Keep the default toolbar font and scaling so the strip comes out about 54 px tall.

Open a Rust tracing JSON .jsonl log, one object per line with timestamp, level, fields{message, five_hour_raw, seven_day_raw} and target, e.g. the ai_agent_dashboard usage_limits poller log also used for main.png. The visible subset must be 75 entries. main.png's session got there with Level: All and Target: aiagent_dashboard_lib::usage_limits, which toolbar-filter.png also shows.

Pick a file or moment where the earliest visible entry is about 10.5 hours old and the latest about 9 minutes old, so the labels read 'First entry: 10 hours 32 minutes ago' and 'Most recent: 9 minutes ago'.
Leave the timestamp labels in relative mode. If they show absolute dates, click 'First entry' once to toggle.
Make the editor wide enough that the toolbar shows all three stats labels without the overflow chevron. main.png was too narrow and cut the strip off after 'Total entries'.
Keep the pointer off the labels so no 'Click to switch between relative and absolute time' tooltip appears.

Capture the toolbar row and crop to the stats segment only: from just left of 'Total entries' to just right of 'Most recent: ... ago', full toolbar height (860x54 in the current file). Crop at the same scale and height as toolbar-panels.png and toolbar-filter.png so the three strips stay a matched series.

screenshots.shows: Dark-theme JSONL editor with the gear popup "JSONL Settings" open under the toolbar's far-left gear icon ("Targets" row hovered, Align = Fields checked). The toolbar is cropped after "Level: All" and the start of "Target". Behind the popup is the Formatted pane of a Rust tracing log from 2026-04-22 (widget starting ... transcript watch failed), with gutter lines 19-21 visible.

steps: Run IntelliJ IDEA with the New UI dark theme and the JSONL Log Viewer plugin installed from this repo.

Open a .jsonl file of Rust tracing-subscriber JSON output from the AI agent dashboard. Its targets are ai_agent_dashboard_lib::{usage_limits,http_server,log_watcher,notifications}, and the common prefix is stripped in the view. Line 1 must be the startup sequence: INFO 'widget starting' (no target), then INFO usage_limits 'usage limits poller started', http_server 'http listening', notifications 'notification manager started'. After that come DEBUG rows ('usage poll success', 'event -> set' / 'event -> clear', 'watching transcript') and one ERROR log_watcher 'transcript watch failed' at line 17. The timestamps are local, around 2026-04-22 14:4x-14:5x.
In the toolbar set Left panel = Formatted and Right panel = Inspect (the Inspect overlay sits off-crop to the right). Set Level = All and Target = (All), and leave the filter empty.

Settings: turn on all seven rendering toggles, set Align = Fields, and turn Scroll to latest on open on. Decide which state to show for Auto-resize inspect height, Soft wrap inspect text and Soft wrap formatted text, which now appear in the popup.
Scroll the Formatted pane to line 1 so that rows 1-21 are visible.
Click the gear icon at the far left of the editor toolbar to open the 'JSONL Settings' popup. Hover the 'Targets' row so it shows highlighted.

Crop from the top-left corner of the editor toolbar (gear icon) to just past the 'Level: All' combo and the start of 'Target'. Vertically, crop down to line 21 of the Formatted pane, so the whole popup is in frame along with the left part of the formatted log and the gutter numbers below the popup. The old crop was about 907x736 px; the popup will now be taller because of the three extra toggles.

screenshots.shows: IntelliJ Settings dialog at Tools > JSONL Log Viewer (dark theme): the plugin's Configurable page with its Formatted view, Behaviour, Field mapping and Colours groups at default values (Align = Targets, decimals 0, paths timestamp/level/target/fields.message/fields), next to the IDE's Settings tree with Tools expanded and "JSONL Log Viewer" selected.

steps: Open the project in IntelliJ IDEA (dark theme, New UI) with the JSONL Log Viewer plugin installed. The subject does not depend on any .jsonl file being open, since the frame is the Settings dialog only.

Reset the plugin settings to defaults (all seven Formatted-view checkboxes on, Align = Targets, Timestamp seconds decimals = 0, paths timestamp / level / target / fields.message / fields), then tick 'Scroll to the latest entry when a .jsonl file is opened' to match the frame.
Open File > Settings (Ctrl+Alt+S), expand Tools in the left tree and select 'JSONL Log Viewer', so the breadcrumb reads 'Tools › JSONL Log Viewer'.
Leave the search box empty and the Align combo closed. Scroll the right-hand panel to the top so 'Formatted view' is the first group and the Colours comment is just visible at the bottom.

Size the dialog so the right pane shows every group from Formatted view down to the Colours comment (about 972x896 px at the capture scale), with the left tree showing Appearance & Behavior through Terminal.
Capture the whole Settings dialog window, title bar and OK/Cancel/Apply footer included, with no desktop around it, and save it as docs/screenshots/settings.png.

screenshots.shows: IntelliJ Settings dialog (dark theme) at Editor > Color Scheme > JSONL Log Viewer, Scheme "Dark", Level group expanded listing all ten attribute keys, with the plugin's five-line demo preview (INFO/DEBUG/WARN/ERROR/TRACE tracing-style lines dated 2026-04-22 14:31:32-46) below.

steps: Run the plugin in IntelliJ IDEA (e.g. the runIde sandbox) with the default dark theme (New UI, Dark editor scheme). No .jsonl file needs to be open because the preview is the plugin's built-in demo text, not a file.
Open Settings (Ctrl+Alt+S) and go to Editor > Color Scheme > JSONL Log Viewer.

Leave Scheme set to "Dark". In the attribute tree, expand the Level group so Debug, Error, Info, Trace and Warn show between Field name and Message. Do not select any attribute, so the right-hand attribute editor stays empty.
Scroll the left settings tree so the sticky "Editor" header shows, with the Color Scheme children from Database down to a partly cut-off TypeScript and the JSONL Log Viewer row highlighted.

Keep the preview pane showing the five demo lines (2026-04-22 14:31:32 INFO http_server: listening addr=127.0.0.1:9077 through 14:31:46 TRACE http_server: trace span span_id=7f3a). The caret line stays on the first line.

Size the Settings dialog so the capture is about 1533x1279 px, then capture the whole dialog window: the title bar ("Settings" plus the close X) at the top and the ?, OK, Cancel and Apply row at the bottom, with nothing cropped inside the dialog.
